definitions: A group of related microcontrollers (MCUs) often sharing architectural similarities, development tools, and peripheral sets, typically offered by a single manufacturer.
A collection of microcontrollers designed to work together or share common characteristics, making them suitable for similar applications or development environments.
examples: The new MCU family offers enhanced security features.
Developers often choose an MCU family based on their project's power requirements.
This MCU family is known for its low-power consumption.
